observations.text: Re-review at 8b6a7f4, delta only. git diff 7ac862b..8b6a7f4 touches six files: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_project_key_length.rs, crates/foundry-core/tests/project_name.rs, the acceptance authority row and its HTML, handoff.json and the published review record. No other oracle or support byte moved, so every observation of the first round other than the two findings stands unchanged and is reused rather than re-run; the tree is clean at 8b6a7f4 (git status --porcelain empty).

Finding 1 is resolved. planted_source now writes one plant, pub const SECOND_COPY, whose text is ProjectKeyError::WrongLength.to_string(), the sentence the product itself gives a refused operator, so a gate clause can pass the scenario only by biting the shipped sentence; no wording is restated in the test and the crafter copy choice no longer decides whether the law is observed. Designer run cited in scratchpad/run4.txt at this revision: the lane compiles with the new foundry_core::ProjectKeyError import, the planted scenarios for the services and store areas fail with the gate ending Some(0) and the summary reads 1 feature, 4 scenarios, 1 passed, 3 failed, 12 steps, 3 failed, so all three areas are RED for the missing clause and the unplanted copy is still accepted with exit 0. The semantic RED and the gate-accepts control are therefore preserved by the fix.

Finding 2 is resolved. a_fallback_address_is_the_lowest_free_candidate now builds the widened key in the body and states its own checkpoint with a WHAT/WHY/HOW message before minting, instead of reaching production through the fixture helper expect("valid key prefix"); the helper stays for the tests that need a fixed key. The file also has its own measured run now, cited from scratchpad/run4.txt: cargo test -p foundry-core --test project_name fails only a_fallback_address_is_the_lowest_free_candidate, 24 passed and 1 failed in 0.07s, with minimal failing input k = "AAAAAAA" and the message naming the seven capital letters and the shipped refusal "project key must be 2-6 characters". That is unambiguous semantic RED, distinguishable from a fixture defect, and within budget.

Amended acceptance row 15 is sound: the stimulus now says the plant carries the very sentence the product gives a refused operator, and the residual blind spot is restated as the gate scope (one planted file per crate, and three crates, while L7 reaches every file those crates hold now or gain later). That matches the declared L7 cases, which are exactly the web, services and store copies, so the amendment narrows no promised outcome and invents no new scope; it replaces a blind spot the fix removed with the one that remains.

Two residual craft-time couplings of the fixed plant, recorded as notes rather than findings because neither removes an observation. First, the plant names the unit variant ProjectKeyError::WrongLength; the design keeps the arms as domain diagnosis and only changes their Display, so the variant stays constructible, but a crafter who gives that variant fields or a new name breaks the acceptance crate build and must return the change to the oracle owner instead of editing the oracle file. Second, the sentence is interpolated into a Rust string literal, so a future refusal wording carrying a quote or backslash would need escaping; the shipped sentence and the designed sentence carry neither.

No check beyond the delta was re-run and none was due: the us-07 oracle feature, its two step files, the core project_key file and the store parity file are byte-identical between 7ac862b and 8b6a7f4, so the reviewer run of the us-07 lane at 7ac862b (exit 101, 47 scenarios, 29 passed, 18 failed, all 18 project-key semantic REDs, scratchpad/review-us07.log) and the host smoke and store observations remain the current evidence for those obligations, cited at their original revision and not restamped. Host smoke at 8b6a7f4 reported by the coordinator: fmt, clippy and check-arch pass and the test step fails only in foundry-core project_key with the same four tests, which is consistent with cargo stopping at the first failing binary and with the project_name run above.
